title: Lung Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison as general references) - the physician decides. Full lung pathway by histology: NSCLC (workup -> clinical stage -> curative local/perioperative therapy with response-adapted adjuvant, unresectable chemoradiation with restaging, and metastatic disease driven by molecular driver -> line-of-therapy sub-trees and PD-L1-directed immunotherapy with sequential later lines), small cell lung cancer (limited / extensive / relapsed with response-adapted consolidation), and malignant pleural mesothelioma (resectable multimodality vs advanced by histology with progression lines). Each treatment leaf routes to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; targeted agents and surgery / radiation without a dose protocol are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Workup / staging / biomarker content is original wording, not proprietary guideline text. Invents no dose / regimen / eligibility criterion. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison), NSCLC / SCLC / Mesothelioma. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Test EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, MET exon-14, RET, NTRK and PD-L1 on every advanced non-squamous NSCLC (and never-smoker / young squamous). An actionable driver takes priority over first-line immunotherapy; do not start a checkpoint inhibitor while molecular results are pending if a targetable driver is plausible.

b.text: After definitive concurrent chemoradiation for unresectable stage III without progression, durvalumab consolidation improves progression-free and overall survival; PD-L1 >= 1% derives the greatest benefit in most regulatory labels.

c.text: For resected EGFR-mutant stage IB-IIIA NSCLC, adjuvant osimertinib prolongs disease-free survival; for resected ALK-positive disease, adjuvant alectinib prolongs disease-free survival. Give targeted adjuvant therapy after any indicated adjuvant chemotherapy.

d.text: In SCLC, obtain brain imaging as part of staging for all patients. After response, consider prophylactic cranial irradiation or MRI surveillance; add consolidative thoracic radiation in selected extensive-stage responders.

e.text: At progression on a targeted agent, re-biopsy (tissue or plasma) before switching therapy. Define the resistance mechanism and exclude histologic transformation (small-cell or squamous), which changes the next regimen.

nodes.name: Histology
nodes.title: Confirmed histology
nodes.description: Lung cancer branches first by histology. Small cell and mesothelioma follow distinct pathways; within NSCLC, squamous vs non-squamous changes the chemotherapy backbone (pemetrexed is non-squamous only) and the breadth of molecular testing.
bullets: NSCLC - non-squamous (adenocarcinoma / large cell): full molecular panel
NSCLC - squamous cell carcinoma
Small cell lung cancer (SCLC)
Malignant pleural mesothelioma

nodes.name: NSCLC workup
nodes.title: NSCLC: workup and staging studies
nodes.description: Establish tissue diagnosis, molecular profile and accurate stage before committing to a curative or palliative track.
bullets: History, physical, smoking and performance status; weight and comorbidity review
Contrast CT chest / upper abdomen; PET-CT for candidates for curative therapy
Brain MRI for stage II or higher, or any neurologic symptom
Pathologic mediastinal staging (EBUS +/- mediastinoscopy) when it changes management

bullets.label: Molecular panel on non-squamous (and selected squamous)
bullets.sub: EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS G12C, MET exon-14, RET, NTRK plus PD-L1 TPS

bullets: Pulmonary function tests before resection or definitive radiation

nodes.name: NSCLC clinical stage
nodes.title: NSCLC: clinical stage / resectability
nodes.description: Select the clinical scenario. Early-stage and resectable locally advanced disease are curative-intent; unresectable stage III is chemoradiation with consolidation; stage IV is molecularly driven palliative therapy.

tables.title: NSCLC stage groups (simplified) and default track
rows: T1-2 N1 or T3 N0 M0
T3-4 N1 or selected N2, M0

nodes.name: Stage I local therapy
nodes.title: Stage I NSCLC: local therapy choice
nodes.description: True stage I disease is cured by local therapy. Fitness for surgery decides between resection and stereotactic radiation.

nodes.name: Stage I resection
nodes.title: Stage I NSCLC: anatomic resection
nodes.description: Curative resection with nodal staging; adjuvant decisions follow from pathology (next step).
bullets: Lobectomy with mediastinal nodal sampling / dissection is the standard
Sublobar resection (segmentectomy / wide wedge) for small peripheral tumors or limited pulmonary reserve
Confirm final pathologic stage and margins; re-resect or add radiation for positive margins
Then decide adjuvant systemic therapy by pathologic risk and driver status (next step)

nodes.name: Stage I SBRT
nodes.title: Stage I NSCLC: stereotactic body radiation
nodes.description: Definitive stereotactic radiation for medically inoperable or surgery-declined early-stage disease.
bullets: Stereotactic body radiation (SBRT) to the primary; regimen by tumor location and size
No surgical nodal staging; ensure PET-CT excludes nodal / distant disease first
No routine adjuvant systemic therapy after SBRT for node-negative disease
Then enter surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Adjuvant after resection
nodes.title: Resected NSCLC: adjuvant systemic therapy
nodes.description: After resection, adjuvant therapy is guided by pathologic risk and by a resected actionable driver. Give any indicated chemotherapy first, then targeted adjuvant therapy.

nodes.name: Adjuvant EGFR
nodes.title: Resected EGFR-mutant NSCLC: adjuvant osimertinib
nodes.description: Adjuvant osimertinib after any indicated adjuvant chemotherapy.
bullets: Adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy for resected stage II-III (and high-risk IB) first
Then adjuvant osimertinib for 3 years for a resected EGFR exon-19del / L858R tumor
Then enter surveillance (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant ALK
nodes.title: Resected ALK-positive NSCLC: adjuvant alectinib
nodes.description: Adjuvant alectinib after any indicated adjuvant chemotherapy.
bullets: Adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy for resected stage II-III first, as indicated
Then adjuvant alectinib for a resected ALK-positive tumor
Then enter surveillance (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant chemo +/- IO
nodes.title: Resected high-risk driver-negative NSCLC: adjuvant chemo +/- immunotherapy
nodes.description: Adjuvant platinum-doublet chemotherapy, with adjuvant immunotherapy for PD-L1-positive tumors per current labels.
bullets: Adjuvant cisplatin-based doublet for resected stage II-III (and high-risk IB)
Pemetrexed doublet for non-squamous; gemcitabine or a taxane doublet for squamous
Consider adjuvant atezolizumab (PD-L1 >= 1%) or pembrolizumab after chemotherapy
Then enter surveillance (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Observation
nodes.title: Resected stage IA NSCLC: observation
nodes.description: No adjuvant systemic therapy for low-risk resected stage IA disease.
bullets: Adjuvant chemotherapy is not indicated for completely resected stage IA disease
Reassess for adjuvant targeted therapy only if a driver was found and residual risk is high
Then enter surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Resectable approach
nodes.title: Resectable stage II-IIIA NSCLC: sequencing
nodes.description: Choose neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy (then surgery, response-adapted adjuvant) or upfront surgery with adjuvant therapy. Withhold perioperative immunotherapy when a targetable EGFR / ALK driver is present.

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant chemo-IO
nodes.title: Resectable NSCLC: neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.description: Neoadjuvant platinum-doublet plus a checkpoint inhibitor, then surgery with pathologic response assessment (next step).
bullets: Neoadjuvant platinum-doublet + a checkpoint inhibitor for 3-4 cycles, then anatomic resection
Pemetrexed doublet for non-squamous; a taxane or gemcitabine doublet for squamous
Do not use perioperative immunotherapy if an EGFR / ALK driver is present - treat those with surgery then adjuvant TKI
Then assess pathologic response and choose adjuvant therapy (next step)
Chemotherapy regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Pathologic response
nodes.title: After neoadjuvant + surgery: pathologic response
nodes.description: Pathologic response to neoadjuvant therapy guides adjuvant intensity. A pathologic complete response predicts excellent outcome; residual disease warrants completing adjuvant systemic therapy.

nodes.name: Adjuvant after pCR
nodes.title: Resectable NSCLC: adjuvant after complete / major response
nodes.description: Complete adjuvant immunotherapy as planned; excellent prognosis.
bullets: Complete the planned adjuvant checkpoint inhibitor (up to about 1 year total perioperative therapy)
Add post-operative radiation only for positive margins or unexpected N2 per multidisciplinary review
Then enter surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Adjuvant after residual
nodes.title: Resectable NSCLC: adjuvant after significant residual disease
nodes.description: Complete adjuvant systemic therapy; escalate by driver and residual burden.
bullets: Complete the planned adjuvant checkpoint inhibitor for driver-negative disease
Add adjuvant chemotherapy if not fully delivered pre-operatively and the patient is fit
Switch to adjuvant osimertinib / alectinib if an EGFR / ALK driver is identified on the resection specimen
Then enter surveillance (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Upfront resection
nodes.title: Resectable NSCLC: upfront resection
nodes.description: Upfront anatomic resection with nodal staging; adjuvant therapy decided from pathology (next step).
bullets: Anatomic (lobectomy) resection with mediastinal nodal dissection
Confirm final pathologic stage, margins and driver status
Then choose adjuvant systemic therapy by risk and driver (next step)

nodes.name: Unresectable III chemoRT
nodes.title: Unresectable stage III NSCLC: concurrent chemoradiation
nodes.description: Definitive concurrent platinum-doublet chemoradiation, then restaging to decide consolidation (next step).
bullets: Concurrent platinum-doublet chemotherapy with thoracic radiation (about 60 Gy in conventional fractionation)
Pemetrexed doublet only for non-squamous; gemcitabine or paclitaxel doublet for squamous
Then restage after chemoradiation to decide consolidation (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Restage after chemoRT
nodes.title: After chemoradiation: restaging and consolidation
nodes.description: Restage after concurrent chemoradiation. Non-progressors receive durvalumab consolidation; an EGFR driver redirects consolidation; frank progression enters the metastatic pathway.

nodes.name: Durvalumab consolidation
nodes.title: Unresectable stage III NSCLC: durvalumab consolidation
nodes.description: Durvalumab consolidation for up to 1 year in patients without progression after chemoradiation.
bullets: Durvalumab consolidation for up to 12 months, ideally started within 6 weeks of chemoradiation
Greatest benefit at PD-L1 >= 1% in most regulatory labels
Then enter surveillance (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: EGFR consolidation
nodes.title: Unresectable stage III EGFR-mutant NSCLC: osimertinib consolidation
nodes.description: For an EGFR-mutant tumor without progression after chemoradiation, osimertinib consolidation is preferred over durvalumab.
bullets: Osimertinib consolidation after chemoradiation for unresectable EGFR-mutant stage III disease
Immunotherapy consolidation is less favored in EGFR-mutant disease (limited benefit, added toxicity)
Then enter surveillance (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Stage III progression
nodes.title: Progression after chemoradiation: treat as metastatic
nodes.description: Frank progression after chemoradiation is treated on the metastatic pathway, directed by molecular driver and PD-L1.
bullets: Re-biopsy and complete molecular profiling if not already done
Enter the metastatic NSCLC pathway (driver-directed, then PD-L1-directed)
Palliative radiation for symptomatic local sites as needed

nodes.name: Actionable driver
nodes.title: Metastatic NSCLC: actionable molecular driver
nodes.description: In stage IV (or recurrent) NSCLC, an actionable driver directs first-line targeted therapy and takes priority over immunotherapy. Choose the dominant driver; if none, proceed to PD-L1.

tables.title: Actionable drivers in metastatic NSCLC and preferred first-line targeted agent

nodes.name: EGFR line
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant metastatic NSCLC: line of therapy
nodes.description: First-line uses a third-generation EGFR TKI. On progression, re-biopsy to define the resistance pattern and pick the next step.

nodes.name: EGFR first line
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant metastatic NSCLC: first-line TKI
nodes.description: A third-generation EGFR TKI is preferred over chemotherapy or immunotherapy first line; reassess at progression (next step).
bullets: Osimertinib is the preferred first-line agent (CNS activity, favorable tolerability)
Consider adding chemotherapy or an amivantamab-based combination for higher-risk disease per current labels
Do not use single-agent immunotherapy in EGFR-mutant disease
At progression, re-biopsy and choose the next step (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: EGFR progression pattern
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant NSCLC: progression pattern
nodes.description: Distinguish oligoprogression (amenable to local therapy while continuing the TKI) from systemic progression, which prompts re-biopsy and a change of systemic therapy.

nodes.name: EGFR oligoprogression
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant NSCLC: oligoprogression
nodes.description: Local therapy to the progressing sites while continuing the effective TKI.
bullets: Stereotactic radiation (or surgery) to the limited progressing sites
Continue osimertinib if systemic disease is otherwise controlled
Escalate to systemic change if further sites progress

nodes.name: EGFR resistance
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant NSCLC: resistance mechanism at systemic progression
nodes.description: Re-biopsy defines the resistance mechanism and directs therapy: a targetable bypass (e.g. MET amplification), histologic transformation, or none identified (platinum chemotherapy).

tables.title: Common EGFR TKI resistance mechanisms and next step

nodes.name: EGFR MET bypass
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant NSCLC: MET-driven resistance
nodes.description: Add a MET inhibitor to the EGFR TKI for MET-amplification bypass resistance. No dedicated MET-inhibitor dose protocol here; regimen shown as guidance.
bullets: Continue osimertinib and add a MET inhibitor per current label / trial for MET-amplified resistance
Amivantamab-based combinations are an alternative for EGFR-dependent resistance
No StewardMD MET-inhibitor dose protocol at present - prescribe per current label
Osimertinib backbone referenced below

nodes.name: EGFR transformation
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant NSCLC: small-cell / squamous transformation
nodes.description: Histologic transformation is treated as its new histology - small-cell transformation gets small-cell chemotherapy.
bullets: Small-cell transformation: platinum-etoposide chemotherapy (as for small cell lung cancer)
Squamous transformation: platinum-taxane / gemcitabine chemotherapy
Continuing the EGFR TKI alongside chemotherapy is reasonable if a targetable EGFR clone persists
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: EGFR chemotherapy
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant NSCLC: platinum chemotherapy after TKI
nodes.description: Platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy when no targetable resistance is found; reassess at further progression (next step).
bullets: Platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy (non-squamous); consider adding a VEGF-pathway agent
An antibody-drug conjugate (e.g. HER3- or TROP2-directed) is an option per current data
Osimertinib remains appropriate only for acquired T790M after an earlier-generation TKI
At further progression, enter the later-line pathway (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: ALK line
nodes.title: ALK-rearranged metastatic NSCLC: line of therapy
nodes.description: A next-generation ALK TKI is preferred first line. On progression, a resistance-guided second TKI or chemotherapy follows.

nodes.name: ALK first line
nodes.title: ALK-rearranged NSCLC: first-line TKI
nodes.description: A next-generation ALK TKI is preferred first line over chemotherapy or immunotherapy; reassess at progression (next step).
bullets: Preferred first-line: alectinib, brigatinib, or lorlatinib (strong CNS penetration)
Avoid single-agent immunotherapy in ALK-positive disease
At progression, re-biopsy for resistance and choose the next step (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: ALK progression
nodes.title: ALK-rearranged NSCLC: after TKI progression
nodes.description: Resistance-guided switch to another next-generation ALK TKI (e.g. lorlatinib), or platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy once TKI options are exhausted.

options.label: Switch to another next-generation ALK TKI

nodes.name: ALK next TKI
nodes.title: ALK-rearranged NSCLC: next-generation TKI switch
nodes.description: Switch to another next-generation ALK TKI guided by the resistance mutation.
bullets: Lorlatinib after progression on a second-generation ALK TKI (broad resistance-mutation coverage)
Choose the agent by the specific ALK resistance mutation where known
Local therapy for isolated CNS or oligoprogression while continuing the TKI
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: ALK chemotherapy
nodes.title: ALK-rearranged NSCLC: chemotherapy after TKIs
nodes.description: Platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy once TKI options are exhausted; reassess at further progression (next step).
bullets: Platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy (non-squamous) after ALK TKIs
Single-agent immunotherapy has limited benefit in ALK-positive disease
At further progression, enter the later-line pathway (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: ROS1 first line
nodes.title: ROS1-rearranged metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: A ROS1 TKI is preferred first line; reassess for a resistance-guided switch or chemotherapy at progression (next step).
bullets: Preferred first-line: entrectinib or repotrectinib (CNS-active); crizotinib is an alternative without CNS disease
Avoid single-agent immunotherapy in ROS1-positive disease
At progression, re-biopsy and choose a next-generation ROS1 TKI or chemotherapy (next step)
Crizotinib dose backbone referenced below

nodes.name: BRAF V600E
nodes.title: BRAF V600E metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: Combined BRAF + MEK inhibition first line; reassess at progression (next step). No dedicated dose protocol here.
bullets: Dabrafenib + trametinib, or encorafenib + binimetinib, for BRAF V600E disease
Chemo-immunotherapy is an alternative if targeted therapy is not tolerated
No StewardMD dose protocol for these combinations - prescribe per current label
At progression, choose a next step (next step)

nodes.name: KRAS G12C
nodes.title: KRAS G12C metastatic NSCLC: therapy
nodes.description: First line is usually chemo-immunotherapy; a KRAS G12C inhibitor is used after prior therapy. Reassess at progression (next step).
bullets: First line: standard PD-L1 / chemo-immunotherapy (KRAS G12C is not yet a first-line target)
After progression: sotorasib or adagrasib (KRAS G12C inhibitors)
No StewardMD dose protocol for KRAS G12C inhibitors - prescribe per current label
Chemo-immunotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: MET exon-14
nodes.title: MET exon-14 skipping metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: A MET inhibitor is preferred first line; reassess at progression (next step). No dedicated dose protocol here.
bullets: Capmatinib or tepotinib for MET exon-14 skipping alterations
Chemo-immunotherapy is an alternative if a MET inhibitor is unavailable
No StewardMD dose protocol for MET inhibitors - prescribe per current label
At progression, choose a next step (next step)

nodes.name: RET fusion
nodes.title: RET-rearranged metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: A selective RET inhibitor is preferred first line; reassess at progression (next step). No dedicated dose protocol here.
bullets: Selpercatinib or pralsetinib for RET fusion-positive disease
Chemo-immunotherapy is an alternative if a RET inhibitor is not tolerated
No StewardMD dose protocol for RET inhibitors - prescribe per current label
At progression, choose a next step (next step)

nodes.name: Targeted progression
nodes.title: Progression on first-line targeted therapy
nodes.description: On progression of a targeted agent (ROS1 / BRAF / KRAS / MET / RET), choose a resistance-guided next-generation inhibitor where available, or transition to platinum chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Next inhibitor
nodes.title: Driver-positive NSCLC: next-generation inhibitor
nodes.description: A resistance-guided next-generation inhibitor where one exists for the driver.
bullets: ROS1: repotrectinib (or lorlatinib) after crizotinib / entrectinib resistance
KRAS G12C: sotorasib or adagrasib after chemo-immunotherapy
BRAF / MET / RET: switch strategy or clinical trial by resistance profile
No StewardMD dose protocol for these agents - prescribe per current label

nodes.name: Driver chemotherapy
nodes.title: Driver-positive NSCLC: platinum chemotherapy
nodes.description: Platinum-doublet chemotherapy once targeted options are exhausted; reassess at further progression (next step).
bullets: Platinum-pemetrexed for non-squamous; platinum-taxane / gemcitabine for squamous
Add immunotherapy selectively (limited benefit in most oncogene-addicted tumors)
At further progression, enter the later-line pathway (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: PD-L1 expression
nodes.title: Driver-negative metastatic NSCLC: PD-L1 tumor proportion score
nodes.description: For driver-negative disease, PD-L1 expression guides single-agent immunotherapy vs chemo-immunotherapy.

nodes.name: PD-L1-high IO
nodes.title: Driver-negative, PD-L1 >= 50%: first-line immunotherapy
nodes.description: Single-agent pembrolizumab is a preferred option; chemo-immunotherapy is an alternative. Reassess at progression (next step).
bullets: Single-agent pembrolizumab (preferred for high PD-L1, good performance status)
Platinum chemo-immunotherapy is a reasonable alternative, especially for bulky / symptomatic disease
Match any chemotherapy backbone to histology (pemetrexed non-squamous only)
At progression, enter the later-line pathway (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.title: Driver-negative, PD-L1 < 50%: first-line chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.description: Platinum chemo-immunotherapy matched to histology. Reassess at progression (next step).
bullets: Non-squamous: pembrolizumab + platinum + pemetrexed
Squamous: pembrolizumab + carboplatin + a taxane
Chemotherapy alone if immunotherapy is contraindicated
At progression, enter the later-line pathway (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Later-line metastatic
nodes.title: Metastatic NSCLC: later-line after platinum-based therapy
nodes.description: After progression on platinum-based (and any targeted / immuno) therapy, choose a later-line cytotoxic, a single agent by tolerance, or best supportive / trial-focused care.

nodes.name: Docetaxel line
nodes.title: Metastatic NSCLC: docetaxel-based later line
nodes.description: Docetaxel with or without an antiangiogenic for fit patients after platinum and immunotherapy.
bullets: Docetaxel, with ramucirumab or nintedanib added for suitable non-squamous patients
An antibody-drug conjugate (e.g. TROP2-directed) is an emerging option per current data
No dedicated StewardMD docetaxel protocol here - prescribe per current label / dose engine

nodes.name: Single-agent line
nodes.title: Metastatic NSCLC: single-agent later line
nodes.description: A single cytotoxic agent chosen by prior exposure, histology and tolerance.
bullets: Single-agent pemetrexed (non-squamous), gemcitabine, or a taxane by prior exposure
Prioritize tolerability and quality of life at later lines
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Best supportive care
nodes.title: Metastatic NSCLC: best supportive care / clinical trial
nodes.description: Symptom-directed care with early palliative-care integration, and clinical trials where available.
bullets: Best supportive and palliative care for poor performance status (ECOG >= 3)
Palliative radiation for symptomatic local sites (bone, brain, airway)
Refer to clinical trials for novel agents where eligible

nodes.name: NSCLC surveillance
nodes.title: NSCLC: surveillance after curative-intent therapy
nodes.description: Follow-up after curative resection or chemoradiation; investigate new symptoms promptly.
bullets: History, physical and contrast CT chest every 6 months for 2-3 years, then annually (annual low-dose CT long-term)
Smoking cessation support at every visit
No routine brain MRI or PET in asymptomatic patients; image on symptoms
Biopsy suspected recurrence and re-profile molecular markers
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence / metastatic disease: enter the driver-directed metastatic pathway

nodes.name: SCLC workup
nodes.title: SCLC: workup and staging
nodes.description: Small cell lung cancer is aggressive and usually disseminated; complete staging including brain imaging drives the limited vs extensive decision.
bullets: History, physical, performance status; paraneoplastic review (SIADH, Cushing, LEMS)
Contrast CT chest / abdomen / pelvis and PET-CT
Brain MRI (or CT) for all patients - CNS involvement is common
Bloods including LDH, sodium and marrow-reserve assessment before chemotherapy

nodes.name: SCLC stage
nodes.title: SCLC: stage
nodes.description: Limited-stage disease fits a tolerable radiation field and is treated with concurrent chemoradiation; extensive-stage adds immunotherapy to chemotherapy; relapse follows a distinct track.

tables.title: SCLC stage and default approach
rows: Confined to one hemithorax / a safe RT field (roughly I-III)
Beyond a tolerable RT field / distant metastases (IV)

nodes.name: Limited-stage SCLC
nodes.title: Limited-stage SCLC: concurrent chemoradiation
nodes.description: Platinum-etoposide with concurrent thoracic radiation; response then guides cranial irradiation (next step).
bullets: Cisplatin (or carboplatin) + etoposide for 4 cycles
Concurrent thoracic radiotherapy started early (twice-daily or high-dose once-daily)
Then reassess response to decide cranial irradiation (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: LS-SCLC response
nodes.title: Limited-stage SCLC: response after chemoradiation
nodes.description: Responders are offered prophylactic cranial irradiation or MRI surveillance; non-response or progression moves to relapse therapy.

nodes.name: SCLC PCI
nodes.title: Limited-stage SCLC: cranial irradiation / surveillance
nodes.description: Prophylactic cranial irradiation or MRI surveillance for responders; then follow-up.
bullets: Prophylactic cranial irradiation for responders, or MRI surveillance as an alternative
Discuss the neurocognitive trade-off of PCI with the patient
Then enter surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: LS-SCLC progression
nodes.title: Limited-stage SCLC: no response / progression
nodes.description: Non-response or progression after chemoradiation is treated on the relapse pathway.
bullets: Restage and confirm progression; treat on the relapsed-SCLC pathway
Assess performance status and goals of care
Palliative radiation for symptomatic sites

nodes.name: Extensive-stage SCLC
nodes.title: Extensive-stage SCLC: chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.description: Platinum-etoposide with an added checkpoint inhibitor; then decide maintenance (next step).
bullets: Carboplatin + etoposide + atezolizumab, or platinum-etoposide + durvalumab, for 4 cycles
Then decide immunotherapy maintenance and local consolidation (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: ES-SCLC maintenance
nodes.title: Extensive-stage SCLC: maintenance vs progression
nodes.description: Non-progressors continue immunotherapy maintenance (with selective thoracic radiation / PCI); progression enters the relapse pathway.

nodes.name: ES-SCLC maintenance
nodes.title: Extensive-stage SCLC: immunotherapy maintenance
nodes.description: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor as maintenance; consider consolidative thoracic radiation and brain management.
bullets: Continue atezolizumab or durvalumab maintenance until progression or intolerance
Consider consolidative thoracic radiation in selected responders
PCI or MRI surveillance for the brain
Then enter surveillance (next step)
Maintenance regimens referenced below

nodes.name: SCLC relapse interval
nodes.title: Relapsed SCLC: interval since platinum
nodes.description: Second-line therapy is guided by the interval since first-line platinum (the chemotherapy-free interval).

nodes.name: Platinum-sensitive relapse
nodes.title: Relapsed SCLC: platinum-sensitive
nodes.description: Re-challenge with the original platinum-etoposide regimen.
bullets: Re-challenge with platinum-etoposide for relapse >= ~6 months after first line
Topotecan or lurbinectedin are alternatives
Reassess goals of care and performance status
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Platinum-resistant relapse
nodes.title: Relapsed SCLC: platinum-resistant
nodes.description: Non-platinum single-agent therapy for early relapse.
bullets: Topotecan or lurbinectedin for relapse < ~6 months after first line
A taxane or other single agent is an alternative
Best supportive care for poor performance status
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: SCLC surveillance
nodes.title: SCLC: surveillance after therapy
nodes.description: Frequent follow-up given the high relapse rate; act quickly on progression.
bullets: History, physical and CT imaging every 2-3 months in year 1, lengthening thereafter
Brain MRI surveillance if PCI was omitted
Smoking cessation support at every visit
nodes.linkLabel: On relapse: enter the relapsed-SCLC pathway

nodes.name: Mesothelioma workup
nodes.title: Mesothelioma: workup and histology
nodes.description: Confirm mesothelioma and its histologic subtype; subtype and resectability drive therapy.
bullets: Asbestos-exposure history; contrast CT chest / abdomen and PET-CT
Adequate tissue (thoracoscopic biopsy preferred) for subtype: epithelioid vs sarcomatoid / biphasic
Pleural fluid cytology alone is insufficient for definitive subtyping
Pulmonary and cardiac function assessment if aggressive surgery is contemplated

nodes.name: Mesothelioma resectability
nodes.title: Mesothelioma: resectable vs advanced
nodes.description: A minority of early epithelioid tumors are candidates for multimodality surgery; most patients present with unresectable disease treated systemically.

nodes.name: Resectable mesothelioma
nodes.title: Resectable mesothelioma: multimodality surgery
nodes.description: Selected early epithelioid disease treated with surgery plus chemotherapy at an experienced center; then decide adjuvant course (next step).
bullets: Macroscopic complete resection (pleurectomy / decortication or extrapleural pneumonectomy) in fit, epithelioid, node-negative patients
Combine with cisplatin-pemetrexed chemotherapy (neoadjuvant or adjuvant) +/- radiation
Manage only at high-volume centers; benefit of aggressive surgery remains debated
Then decide adjuvant course by tolerance / response (next step)
Chemotherapy regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Mesothelioma adjuvant
nodes.title: Resectable mesothelioma: adjuvant course
nodes.description: Complete perioperative chemotherapy and radiation as planned, or move to the progression pathway if disease recurs.

nodes.name: Mesothelioma adjuvant therapy
nodes.title: Resectable mesothelioma: completed multimodality therapy
nodes.description: Complete perioperative chemotherapy and hemithoracic radiation, then structured follow-up.
bullets: Complete cisplatin-pemetrexed chemotherapy (if not fully delivered pre-operatively)
Hemithoracic radiation in selected patients at experienced centers
Structured CT follow-up; treat recurrence on the advanced pathway
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Mesothelioma histology
nodes.title: Advanced mesothelioma: histologic subtype
nodes.description: Subtype guides the first-line choice between chemotherapy and dual immunotherapy; non-epithelioid tumors derive greater relative benefit from immunotherapy.

nodes.name: Advanced epithelioid mesothelioma
nodes.title: Advanced epithelioid mesothelioma: first-line systemic therapy
nodes.description: Either platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy or nivolumab-ipilimumab is acceptable first line; reassess at progression (next step).
bullets: Cisplatin (or carboplatin) + pemetrexed, with the option to add a VEGF inhibitor
Nivolumab + ipilimumab is an alternative first-line option
